topSignals.text: BE traded $219.21-$237.45 and closed at $228.11 (+$9.79), extending the Pelosi-disclosure rally flagged August 25-27. The two analyst upgrades cite margin gains and roughly $27B in financing capacity (unverified, see LCOE section) - the first dated catalyst beyond the Pelosi trade and the Q2 beat-and-raise. Motley Fool | StockAnalysis

topSignals.title: Texas's ERCOT data-center audit gets hard numbers for the first time in this digest: up to 300 projects, ~200 GW of future demand - double ERCOT's own peak-demand record - under review through roughly December 10.
topSignals.text: Gov. Abbott's August 3 order paused new ERCOT interconnection studies pending a PUCT/ERCOT verification sweep; the August 14 ERCOT board meeting confirmed the scope and a "less than nine months" completion target, consistent with the December 10 date reported directly by Utility Dive. Under 10% of audited data centers were found compliant with existing power/water reporting law. This digest has carried "ERCOT audit, targeted completion December 2026" as a pending item since August 22 without noting the scale - useful context for behind-the-meter SOFC's core pitch (skip the queue) in the US's second-largest data-center market. Utility Dive | Texas Tribune

topSignals.title: Correction to this digest's standing framing: FERC's large-load interconnection reform is a nationwide six-RTO action, not a PJM-specific one.
topSignals.text: FERC's June 18 show-cause orders went to all six FERC-jurisdictional grid operators - PJM, MISO, SPP, CAISO, ISO-NE and NYISO - not PJM alone, as this digest's PJM-centric coverage (BYONG, the Reliability Backstop Procurement) has implied since mid-August. All six filed responses by the August 17 deadline; a 30-day intervenor-comment window is now open on each. The "avoid the interconnection queue" value driver this digest has so far priced only against PJM benchmarks (the $555/MW-day backstop cap, August 26) likely applies in the other five territories too, each on its own timeline and price. Akin Gump | FERC.gov

lcoe.text: FERC's nationwide scope broadens the "avoided interconnection queue" benefit driver (see Top Signal #3): the LCOE model's avoided-cost-of-grid-connection benefit side has so far been anchored only to PJM benchmarks (the $555/MW-day backstop cap, August 26). With MISO, SPP, CAISO, ISO-NE and NYISO now under the same FERC show-cause reform, the same benefit driver plausibly applies in those territories too, each with its own price/timeline once individual tariff reforms are approved - worth a multi-RTO version of that calculation rather than a PJM-only one.

Texas scale numbers as a queue-pressure proxy (see Top Signal #2): ~200 GW of Texas data-center demand sitting behind an audit with no firm restart date (targeted within nine months of August 14, i.e. by roughly May 2027, with December 10, 2026 reported as the specific ERCOT target) is a concrete, large-market illustration of the multi-year interconnection delay that behind-the-meter SOFC is priced against - useful as a qualitative anchor even without a dollar figure attached.

Bloom Energy's "~$27B financing capacity" (✎ as reported by Motley Fool, not independently verified): if accurate, a data point on capital availability for SOFC deployment financing at scale; flagged for confirmation before use.
Gas price case: EIA's August STEO figures ($3.44/MMBtu 2026 average, $2.87/MMBtu Q3, $3.03/MMBtu remaining five months) unchanged, no new revision today.

Pending carry-forward: PJM Expedited Interconnection Track confirmation, FERC RM26-4 comment window (~September 16), intervenor-comment windows now open on all six RTOs' show-cause filings (30 days from August 17, i.e. ~September 16), NMED/State Engineer Project Jupiter Supreme Court response (September 2), Bloom 10-Q (September 11), Bloom scandium class-action deadline (September 28), FCEL Q3 call (September 2), Ceres H1 2026 results (September, unconfirmed date), Bloom Q3 earnings (October 27), Rolls-Royce SMR GDA DAC (Q4 2026/Q1 2027 estimate), Germany EnEfG Bundestag/Bundesrat vote (autumn 2026), Texas ERCOT audit completion (~December 10, 2026).
